note.question: Why do fixed costs matter for proof-of-work–based cryptocurrencies?
note.overview: We assess how the cost structure of cryptocurrency mining affects the response of miners to exchange rate fluctuations and the immutability of cryptocurrency ledgers that rely on proof-of-work. The paper shows that the amount of mining power supplied to currencies that rely on specialized hardware, such as Bitcoin, responds less to adverse exchange rate shocks than other currencies respond to such shocks, a fact that is instrumental to avoiding double-spending attacks. For smaller currencies with low exchange rate correlation, transferability eliminates the protection that fixed costs provide.
